Content: A student is cooking with a type of plant called thyme and notices that thyme has a fragrant smell. The student wonders how this smell is produced and does some research. The student learns that the smell produced by thyme is due to oils that the plant produces. Some types of thyme plants produce oils with different chemicals that affect the plant’s smell.

Thyme plants that produce oils with stronger-smelling chemicals, like phenols, deter predators from eating the thyme plants. However, having this phenol trait also makes these plants more likely to perish from freezing temperatures than thyme plants without phenols.

The student finds a data table that shows the `text(percentage)` of thyme plants with the phenolic trait and nonphenolic trait in `text(1974)` and `text(2010)` in a region of France where these thyme plants grow.
The student also finds a graph that shows how the average `text(annual)` winter temperature changed over time from `text(1955)-text(2009)` in this region of France where thyme plants grow.
